candidate.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13/PDF p.17: focused assessment, diagnostic-test monitoring and recognition of treatment/condition complications
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — diagnostic interpretation and complication recognition
candidate.educational_objective: After a hospital fall, use a post-fall review to identify contributing factors and update the individualized prevention plan.

options.A: Keep the existing plan unchanged because a fall proves that patient-specific reassessment cannot improve prevention.
options.B: Delete the prior risk assessment and use the same standard fall bundle for every client after any fall.
options.C: Focus only on documenting the incident; the prevention plan should not change unless the fall caused a major injury.
options.D: Conduct a post-fall review with the care team to identify contributing factors and revise the individualized prevention plan based on what changed or failed.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ PSNet fall-prevention guidance identifies a post-fall review as an opportunity for secondary prevention and emphasizes individualized fall-prevention plans that respond to each patient’s risk factors, needs, and preferences. After immediate injury assessment, a team review of contributing factors and revision of the individualized plan best supports preventing another fall.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Post-fall review supports secondary prevention, and fall-prevention plans should be individualized and responsive to patient-specific risk factors.
candidate.source_locator: Section 'Preventing Falls in Healthcare Settings' — individualized plans and multidisciplinary responsibility; post-fall review as an opportunity for secondary prevention.
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) — PSNet
candidate.source_version_date: UC Davis PSNet Editorial Team update 2024-06-15; primer last reviewed in 2024; live AHRQ PSNet page rechecked 2026-08-16.
candidate.stem: A hospitalized client falls despite an existing prevention plan. After the nurse assesses the client and addresses immediate injury concerns, which safety action best supports preventing a recurrence?
